subject.title: autoreview: secret-scanner false positives on identifier and member-expression values (e.g. `apiSecret: ctx.cloudinary.apiSecret`)

question: Should autoreview accept only explicitly verified JavaScript/TypeScript reference roots and fixture values, or treat every syntactically pure identifier/member expression as non-literal?
rationale: Both approaches reduce false positives, but they define different fail-closed guarantees for a scanner that protects review bundles from secret disclosure.

options.title: Keep verified narrow references
options.body: Rebase and extend the dialect-scoped allowlist only for reproduced roots and exact fixtures, with regression tests for the issue examples.

options.title: Accept all source references
options.body: Allow any parsed identifier or member expression in JavaScript/TypeScript and rely on the remaining literal and token detectors.

options.title: Add an explicit override
options.body: Preserve current scanning by default and separately design a reviewed redaction or override workflow for blocked bundles.

recommendation.title: Keep verified narrow references
recommendation.body: Rebase and extend the dialect-scoped allowlist only for reproduced roots and exact fixtures, with regression tests for the issue examples.

likelyOwner.reason: The current parser-backed security boundary originates in the merged implementation they authored.
